verdicts.reason: A has a sensible structure: a large product on the left, then headline, subhead and CTA stacked on the right. But the SOLSTICE wordmark renders broken ('SOLST CE'), and the headline runs across the busy translucent circle almost to the right edge. B shrinks the product to a tiny thumbnail jammed against the left edge, and the CTA nearly touches 'hour', so they fight for attention. B also leaves the whole bottom third of the canvas empty.

B is a clean rearrangement for the taller banner. The logo, headline, subhead and CTA share one left edge, and the product sits large inside the circle on the right with clear hierarchy. Its only weakness is that the logo is small. A shrinks the product to a tiny sticker at the left edge and crowds the CTA against the headline. A also leaves a large dead band below the subhead.

A has the same flaws as before: the can is shrunk to a thumbnail, the CTA almost collides with the headline, and the bottom of the canvas is empty. B keeps the original left-to-right order, but the headline is oversized and wraps over two lines. In B the subhead is jammed under the headline and leaves 'small batches.' alone on its second line. B's logo is also tiny and isolated far to the left, and the product is small. Its CTA has no collision, though, so B is marginally less broken.
